subject: Academic Rigor for Students With Disabilities
overview: School Committee member Melanie Perkins McLaughlin outlined her objectives for her new term, emphasizing academic rigor for students with disabilities and expanded community outreach. The discussion also covered the role of school subcommittees and the results of recent policy decisions regarding family engagement.

items.title: MLK Day Acknowledgment
items.summary: The host acknowledged Martin Luther King Day and read a poem by Medford's Poet Laureate Terry E. Carter in observance of the holiday.

items.title: Election and Inauguration Reflections
items.summary: Melanie Perkins McLaughlin reflected on the challenges of the recent election cycle and the impact of the global pandemic on municipal governance.

items.title: Priorities for the New Term
items.summary: McLaughlin identified her primary focus areas as improving representation for underrepresented communities and ensuring academic rigor for students with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

items.title: Community Listening Sessions
items.summary: To address representation gaps, McLaughlin announced plans to hold regular listening sessions at churches and community venues to better understand barriers to participation.

items.title: Role of Subcommittees and Community Involvement
items.summary: McLaughlin explained the function of school committee subcommittees and encouraged residents to engage with specific bodies such as the Special Education and Behavioral Health Subcommittee.

items.title: Special Education Advancements
items.summary: The discussion reviewed the history of the Special Education Parent Advisory Council and the ongoing implementation of a district-wide disability awareness curriculum pilot.

items.title: Bullying and Family Engagement Audit
items.summary: McLaughlin discussed the persistence of bullying issues and noted that the School Committee voted not to continue a state-led family engagement audit project this year due to competing priorities.
